key_catalyst: Trump's operational Strait of Hormuz blockade with a 20% cargo toll and a third night of US strikes on Iran, pushing Brent above $85
reasoning: The Hormuz catalyst has escalated from Monday's 'closure fears' (2026-07-13, QQQ -1.90%) into an operational blockade with a 20% cargo toll, a third night of strikes, Brent up ~9.6% above $85, and commercial transit collapsed to three vessels per 24 hours — a materially worse fact set that the +0.95% pre-market bounce is treating as a dip-buy. Recent history shows this exact misread being punished: on 2026-07-10 the market rallied because Iranian retaliation was 'judged contained' with Brent falling to $76, and the next session gave back -1.90%. Meanwhile the AI-capex leg that powered 2026-07-09 (+1.66%) and 2026-07-10 (+0.31%) — Micron's $250B plan and an oversubscribed SK Hynix IPO — is unwinding, with SK Hynix down a record 15.37% and the SOX off 4.78%, so the bounce rests almost entirely on a CPI print that has not yet landed.
